was: Larimer County open space ~2 mi SE of Estes Park, 7,880-8,964 ft, ponderosa forest and meadows; no water recreation on site (Lake Estes is 3 mi away). Bobcat (campground #2) is the RV campground; Hermit's Hollow (#1) sites cap at 20 ft, Kruger (#3) is equestrian. --Claude

was: Larimer County campground on the northeast end of Pinewood Reservoir west of Carter Lake (~6,580 ft), part of the Colorado-Big Thompson Project. The county warns the only access is a narrow 4-mile paved road with 8-10% grades and that most sites are small, not recommended for larger RVs and motorhomes. Drinking water runs April-August only; the nearest frost-free spigot is at Flatiron Campground, 4 miles east. Boat ramp closed: hand-launched craft only, no swimming. A daily vehicle entrance permit is required on top of the camping fee. --Claude

was: NGPC recreation area on a Logan Creek/Elkhorn oxbow off US 275, ~4 mi north of Scribner, beside Powder Horn WMA. Electric sites in a loop at the south end of the oxbow; the four primitive sites have been closed by flood damage. Self-pay envelopes. Primitive restrooms. --Claude

was: NGPC SRA on the 2,158-acre Lake Minatare NE of Scottsbluff. Lake View campground runs along the west arm on the peninsula by the office: paved back-ins in a cottonwood belt, part bookable online, the rest first come. West Wind has basic sites, and there is non-designated beach and primitive camping. The Butte View campground across the lake is its own entry. Plains Lighthouse, boat ramps. A wildlife refuge, closed to all public access October 15 - January 15. --Claude

was: Lone Eagle campground of Lake McConaughy SRA, on the north shore off Shoreline Road (Arthur Bay Gate 2 or Sandy Beach Gate 4 off Highway 92): a paved loop of full hookup back-ins, its south-west row behind a line of trees above the wide sand beach. Beach camping on the sand is separate and booked 30 days ahead. --Claude

was: Modern electric loop at Swanson Reservoir SRA near Trenton: 47 RV sites with 20/30/50-amp hookups, modern restrooms and showers, two dump stations; shaded sites set back in the canyon (the sandy-beach primitive areas are separate loops). Reservable on ReserveAmerica up to 180 days ahead (25 Spring Canyon sites listed there in 2026). Park entry permit required. --Claude

was: Nebraska National Forest (Bessey Ranger District) campground at Halsey, in the historic hand-planted Bessey forest. Loops of pine-shaded pads, most with electric; a group site and tent-only sites besides. Showers and flush restroom mid-May to mid-October; winter water only at the recreation building. The Middle Loup River (tubing, canoeing) and a 7-acre stocked pond are nearby, but the loops sit back in the trees, not on the water. ATVs may ride from the sites to the trailhead. --Claude

was: Adams County Fairgrounds camping at 947 South Baltimore, Hastings, with 396 hookup sites: 20 back-in full-service sites south of the grandstands (upgraded to 50/30 amp in 2021), 86 water-and-electric and 290 electric-only, plus a tent field, a shower house and a dump station at the entrance that takes free-will donations.  The campground is seasonal, opening and closing with the weather, and closes to the public during several fairground events.  RV stays are limited to three weeks and tent stays to one, and campfires aren't allowed. --Claude

was: City of Fremont campground at the Christensen Field complex, outside the Main Arena. The West Campground is open to the public; the East Campground's 20 pedestals are for special events only. Campers may have to move or leave for a scheduled event. No tents. --Claude

was: City of Genoa park (Nance County). A few gravel/grass sites with 30-amp electric and water on the camping loop at the south side of the park, beside the pool and ball fields; a wooded creek channel runs beyond the loop road. Pay at the city offices. --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night in July 2024 (RV Life review: the city raised it from $10); the city's pages post no rate (2026-10-11). --Claude

was: Village of Lynch RV park on the south side of town (4th St & Railroad Ave), a short walk from the main street; Ponca Creek is beyond the trees to the south-east. Back-in gravel pads in grass with tables and fire pits, a covered picnic area. Pay at a bar downtown or call for pickup; Grass can be long and neighbouring dogs noisy (2024 review). CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night in July 2024 (The Dyrt and Campendium reviews); the village has no web page (2026-11-05). --Claude

was: York County fairgrounds at 2345 Nebraska Ave, with camping open to the public outside fair week as well. Gridded angled pull-in pads; a dump site nearby. Fair-week spots are booked through the county extension office. --Claude

was: Campground on a private ~10-acre lake between I-80 (Exit 179) and the Platte River at North Platte. Pull-throughs for any size RV, plus primitive and tent areas along the lake. Swimming beaches, catch-and-release fishing with no permit needed, and kayak and paddle-boat rentals. Off-season (Oct 1-Apr 14) is self-registration at the office dropbox, with water only at sites H-X and no showers. Reservations by phone with a $10 deposit. --Claude

was: Small private campground next to Carhenge north of Alliance, with views across open country. All pull-through sites on a slight hill in full sun; most need side-to-side levelling, and hookups are spread out at many sites. Self check-in kiosk, pay cash in an envelope. Full-hookup, water-only and no-hookup sites, 3rd consecutive night half price. Campers report no bathhouse; porta-johns for tents. --Claude
